I've been calling for over 15 minutes to schedule an appointment and no one is answering...

My experience at this clinic was extremely negative and disappointing.

I arrived at the clinic around 8:50 am with my dog, who was unwell and subsequently vomiting in the reception area. Despite it being a veterinary hospital with an emergency service, I remained waiting and, by 9:45 am, I had not been seen nor had my dog ​​received any evaluation.

The most infuriating thing was seeing my animal vomiting and unwell in the reception area and, even so, there was no intervention or initial assessment by the staff.

When, faced with the delay and concerned about my dog's condition, I informed them that I would leave to seek other care, the employee simply did not respond. In an emergency situation, when we are distressed and seeking help for a debilitated animal, I consider this behavior completely unacceptable.

If a clinic presents itself as an emergency veterinary hospital, I expect at least a triage and proper guidance when an animal arrives visibly ill.

I left there deeply indignant and worried about my dog. I do not recommend this establishment. When we most need support and assistance, we cannot simply be left waiting while our animal is suffering.

I hope the clinic's management becomes aware of this situation and reviews its service procedures so that other animals and their owners do not have to go through the same experience.

After 24 hours of hospitalization, we continued treatment at home. Unfortunately, a few days later, Sonic's condition worsened significantly. We tried to get to the hospital in time, but we couldn't. Our beloved Sonic died in the car on the way to the hospital.
When we arrived, the nurse and Dr. Ana reacted immediately, but unfortunately there was nothing that could be done. We will never forget how they treated us, with so much affection, humanity, empathy, and compassion, during such a painful time for us.

My dog ​​was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection by a doctor at this clinic. An antibiotic was prescribed, and the dog started to improve, but almost at the end of the course, the dog got worse again (she started urinating blood, wasn't eating, and was very lethargic).
I took my dog ​​back to this clinic around 10 pm and she was only seen at 2 am.
The doctor who saw me was the only doctor present at the clinic; she seemed nervous, as several people were already complaining in the waiting room.
My dog ​​had tests done, and the doctor said she had a urinary tract infection. However, she said her kidney function wasn't affected. I asked her to change the antibiotic and even asked to see the file, including the urine culture I had done about 15 days earlier, but it was no use. She said she wasn't going to change her colleague's prescription, that she would contact her because she was on vacation, and that she would get back to me later. I left the clinic with my dog, just as she had arrived, urinating blood, very lethargic, and without any prescription. They told me to continue taking the same antibiotic. I waited all day for them to contact me, I called the clinic and nothing. My dog ​​ended up passing away.

We went there urgently on the night of August 15th with my Schnauzer because she had a urinary tract infection. We waited 4 hours to be seen, and the only veterinarian on duty that entire night only did some tests and sent us away without prescribing antibiotics. We insisted on antibiotics or something for the pain, which the doctor refused and didn't even bother to consider – she just told us to come back in 2 days if it got worse. TERRIBLE SERVICE!!! Don't go there, poor animals if they get sick at night – inexperienced doctors, just scheduling appointments, a disgrace! My dog ​​died two days later because of this clinic!!!!!! A disgrace!!!!!!!!

I do not recommend this hospital to anyone!
In desperation, I went to this hospital, and in the first few minutes of treatment, I got the impression that what motivates them is money. They don't answer questions ("I don't know"), and for every question asked, the solution found is that it's necessary to do tests, tests, and more tests without ever giving a price, and wanting to do them all at once and not by eliminating parts... Fortunately - just as the vet was getting ready to leave with the kitten - I was in time to ask how much everything would cost, and seeing a bill I couldn't pay, they agreed to do the essential tests, but with the "scolding" that I could look for a cheaper clinic! Anyway... I know they see animals suffering every day, but the coldness with which they give news is atrociously insensitive (I admit I was very emotional and that this may be disturbing for the professional, but still...). They wanted to schedule a new appointment, which I didn't make, saying they would call later to let me know about my kitten's condition.
I called countless times for a week; the recording itself ends the call after 18 minutes. When they answered, they said the veterinarian who treated me in the emergency room would call me: to this day, nothing, and today another 36 minutes of waiting on the phone in vain.
But as everything has a happy ending, I was recommended to a clinic that I thought, after this, was impossible to exist: offices designed for animals and owners, service from people who care about and pamper animals, someone who listens to what is said and doesn't dismiss it, someone who doesn't look at the clock and "feels" our pain, someone who says, "there's no need for more...". And all for €27 a consultation!
May the veterinary NHS come quickly....

My dog ​​has been a client of this clinic since he was 2 months old, since the day he came into my care, back when it was still the Santa Marinha Veterinary Hospital. During that time, my dog ​​was always well attended to, well treated, and cared for, and I always received the necessary information from the clinic about everything that happened to my dog. I even had the right to photos of when my dog ​​was there for training and the staff would carry him around. At no point did I feel that money was more important than the animal. I always recommended the hospital to family, friends, neighbors, etc...
Unfortunately, at this moment I cannot say the same about the hospital, the service, the new doctors and staff.

My dog ​​has been having flare-ups of problems that were diagnosed years ago when he was still at Santa Marinha. Now I had to return in distress, trying to get him the medication he needed. I went back because my dog's entire medical history is there, and because of the affection I have for the staff and the old team that remained. I agreed to be seen by a new doctor, I gave her the opportunity, and I left dissatisfied. She simply didn't listen to me, didn't look at the animal's history, they did two or three x-rays, all the same, heart and lung exams if I'm not mistaken, and they prescribed the inhaler for my dog, when I knew he needed corticosteroids. I returned a few days later when they did the third x-ray, and that's when the doctor told me she thought my dog ​​had exactly what I described in the first consultation, but still thought I should do an endoscopy, something invasive considering it would require general anesthesia and my dog ​​is already 10 years old. This diagnosis was probably just to confirm what I said initially. I asked A quote was given, and they said they would think about it because it doesn't make sense to do an exam that doesn't tell me anything new, that is expensive, and that, considering the animal's age and weight, it wasn't justified. However, I left without any medication, without them being able to give me any certainty about what was wrong with my dog, and I went home waiting for the doctor to send me a quote so I could decide whether or not to do the exam, a quote that never arrived, even after I called the hospital again to ask for it.

In conclusion, I spent money, left without any certainty, and in the end, it was supposedly what I said it was, but the doctor still had doubts and wanted me to spend more money. During this time, my dog ​​got worse, and they recommended Dr. Ana to me, whom I decided to try and give a chance, and she is completely different. The service was spectacular. They were able to review my dog's medical history, which the other doctor said wasn't possible, and only prescribed medication, saying that all the tests the other doctor requested weren't worthwhile since we already knew the diagnosis. I also managed to get my dog ​​to finally receive his overdue vaccinations, which he missed last time due to the potential tests he might have to undergo.
However, with the heat, my dog ​​hasn't been doing well, and I need to speak with the doctor to adjust his medication and everything else. Every time I call the hospital to try to speak with Dr. Ana, the response is always the same standard one: "Bring the dog here."
I am dissatisfied not with Dr. Ana because she was extremely humble, realistic, took into account my dog's age and weight, and didn't try to extort money just for the sake of it, and I'm also not with the staff who were there before who know my dog ​​and continue to treat him well, but I have a lot to say about the new staff who have joined. At this moment I do not recommend the hospital to anyone, and let it be clear that my whole family takes their animals there and nobody is happy, we all have the same opinion. Hence my displeasure, the prices have increased and the concern is no longer the animals.

I have already made it clear that I do not want to be treated by Dr. Beatriz again and that is certain.

Thank you for everything.

I contacted your telephone line beforehand, where I was informed that I could bring my dog ​​in immediately, as he needed urgent observation due to his health condition. I was also assured that, as soon as I arrived at the clinic, I would be seen promptly.
Trusting this information, I went to the clinic immediately. However, upon arrival, I took a number and waited for more than 20 minutes to be called. When I was finally seen at reception, it was necessary to register my data and the animal's, including presenting the vaccination record, as it was the first time I was using your services. I only went to your clinic because my dog's usual veterinarian is on vacation and AniCura Santa Marinha was recommended to me by acquaintances.
After this administrative procedure, I again waited for about 20 minutes, at which point I was informed that the information provided by the telephone line was incorrect. In the end, my dog ​​could be seen, but he would have to wait like any other patient, contrary to what I had been assured.
When he was finally examined, I was informed that tests would be necessary, as it was not possible to determine the cause of the problem through clinical observation. This was followed by another wait of about 20 to 30 minutes for the tests to be carried out and the results to be obtained.
The most worrying thing is that, after all this process, I was not given any concrete explanation about what my dog ​​has. He was only prescribed paracetamol — medication that, curiously, I had been told earlier on the phone line not to administer — as well as an anti-inflammatory. I was also told that I should return on Friday for a new consultation and reassessment.
It is important to mention that my dog ​​was taken to the clinic because he was lethargic and had a fever of 40.1°C at home, reaching 40.5°C at your facilities. Given that this is a high and potentially worrying temperature, I expected a faster, clearer and more effective response.

What displeased me most in this whole situation was leaving the clinic without understanding what was happening with my dog. As a pet owner, it is extremely distressing to see an animal that is part of the family debilitated, with a high fever and without its usual behavior, and to receive only medication to control the symptoms without any concrete explanation about the possible origin of the problem or a more clarifying action plan.
In the end, I was charged €180, without being presented with any diagnosis or conclusion about the animal's clinical condition, with the recommendation limited to symptomatic medication and the scheduling of a new appointment.
I consider that both the administrative service and the clinical follow-up fell far short of the expectations one expects from a reference veterinary clinic. The contradictory information provided by the telephone line, the excessive waiting times, the lack of communication and the absence of adequate clarifications left me deeply dissatisfied.
Given the entire situation described, I regret to inform you that I have lost confidence in the services provided by this clinic. My experience fell far short of what I expected from a veterinary clinic with AniCura's reputation, and therefore I do not intend to use your services again in the future. Similarly, I will not feel comfortable recommending the clinic to family, friends, or acquaintances, given how this situation was handled.
Veterinary hospital of reference for the handling of emergency cases.

There are moments in life when words seem insufficient to express our gratitude. Today, I write to publicly and deeply deservedly acknowledge two entities that have decided to join forces for animal welfare: the Santa Marinha Veterinary Hospital and the Patinhas Sem Lar association.

Your collaboration and the work you do together, side by side with temporary and permanent families, is simply extraordinary. It is a humanism, a love, and a dedication that restores our faith in goodness.

Seeing this chain working is inspiring: from the tireless work of the association's volunteers to the dedication of the entire hospital team – reception, assistants, and veterinarians. Everyone works in perfect harmony, with a huge commitment to giving their best and saving lives.

I want to thank you from the bottom of my heart for the support and work you did for me and my dear Alice. She, unfortunately, passed away, but until her last breath she was incredibly well treated, cared for, and loved by this great family you form.

A very special and heartfelt thank you to Dr. Daniela Martins. Her dedication was total. She was tireless, present, caring, and demonstrated an empathy and sensitivity that I will never forget. In such a difficult moment, knowing that Alice was surrounded by your shield of love brought me immense peace.

Saying "thank you" seems insufficient for the magnitude of your daily commitment. You don't just care for animals; you comfort hearts and change lives together.

Thank you for existing and for this beautiful partnership, Santa Marinha Veterinary Hospital and Patinhas Sem Lar. You are incredible! 🙏✨
